In old mice, the treatment reversed naturally occurring cartilage loss and protected animals from developing arthritis after ACL-like

title: Two-year trial: diet soft drinks match water for weight loss
summary: A two-year randomized trial of 493 adults found diet soft drinks sweetened with aspartame, acesulfame-K, or sucralose produced weight loss comparable to water (4.8 kg vs 3.7 kg), with both groups maintaining reductions and showing no clinically meaningful metabolic differences.
takeaways: Diet beverages lost 4.8 kg vs 3.7 kg for water over 104 weeks
No significant differences in blood pressure, cholesterol, or metabolic biomarkers
Both groups sustained weight loss through year two without behavioral support
Sweetener consumption remained within European Food Safety Authority thresholds
Published in British Journal of Nutrition

title: Incremental lifestyle improvements could significantly extend lifespan
summary: A new study suggests that small improvements in sleep, nutrition, and exercise together could meaningfully increase human lifespan.

title: Creatine supplementation helps middle-aged adults build muscle and strength even without structured exercise
summary: A 12-week study of adults aged 45–65 found that creatine monohydrate supplementation increased lean tissue and strength gains independently of exercise, and when combined with resistance training and calorie restriction, produced greater strength improvements while preserving muscle during fat loss.
takeaways: Creatine-only group (no exercise) gained ~2.4 pounds of lean tissue and increased leg press and bench press strength over 12 weeks
Exercise + creatine group experienced greater gains in leg press strength, bench press strength, and time to exhaustion compared to exercise + placebo
Exercise + diet + creatine group added nearly 3 pounds of lean tissue while losing fat mass; placebo group showed little change in lean tissue
Study involved 64 healthy adults aged 45–65 published in Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition

title: High-Intensity Interval Training Preserves Muscle While Reducing Fat in Older Adults
summary: A six-month randomized trial of 123 older adults found high-intensity interval training (HIIT) reduced body fat while preserving lean muscle, whereas moderate-intensity training caused modest fat loss with slight muscle decline.
takeaways: 123 healthy older adults, average age 72, BMI 26 kg/m²
Six-month study with three supervised 45-minute gym sessions weekly
HIIT reduced fat without lean muscle loss; moderate-intensity caused small lean mass decline
Both high and moderate intensity significantly reduced fat vs. low-intensity control

title: Meta-analysis finds dairy trans fats pose no heart disease or diabetes risk
summary: A meta-analysis of 22 studies found that naturally occurring trans fats in dairy products do not increase risk of heart disease, stroke, or type 2 diabetes. The distinction is critical—industrial trans fats remain harmful, while dairy trans fats showed no adverse effects.
takeaways: 22-study meta-analysis examined dairy trans fats
10 controlled trials: participants consumed 1.3–13.2g trans fat daily
12 long-term cohorts: up to two decades, no adverse associations
Natural dairy trans fats differ from harmful industrial trans fats

title: Single factor emerges as stronger longevity predictor than diet or exercise
summary: A study published in Sleep Advances found that insufficient sleep (less than seven hours nightly) was a stronger predictor of longevity than diet or exercise when analyzing county-level survey data from 2019 to 2025. Only smoking had a stronger association with life expectancy; the unexpected streng
takeaways: Insufficient sleep (<7 hours/night) stronger predictor of longevity than diet or exercise
Only smoking had stronger association with life expectancy in first model
County-level US survey data, 2019–2025, controlled for physical inactivity, employment, education
Sleep physiologist Andrew McHill: correlation strength was unexpected
Observational study; cannot prove causation; recommends 7–9 hours nightly

title: Vitamin D analog shows promise in pancreatic cancer clinical trial
summary: A small clinical trial found paricalcitol, a vitamin D analog, safely combined with chemotherapy in metastatic pancreatic cancer, reduced fibroblast activation, and showed encouraging signals including higher treatment response rates and improved one-year progression-free survival in patients with h
takeaways: Paricalcitol reduced fibroblast activation in tumor microenvironment
Patients receiving paricalcitol + chemotherapy showed more treatment responses
High vitamin D receptor tumors had longest overall survival
Published in Nature Cancer; built on Salk Institute laboratory findings
Targets protective fibrotic environment to sensitize tumors to therapy

summary: A nutrition study demonstrates that combined intake of sodium bicarbonate and carbohydrates significantly improves athletic performance metrics.

title: Study finds strength training shrinks fat cells in mice within seven days
summary: Seven days of strength training sessions in obese mice triggered shrinkage of visceral fat cells and reactivated fat-burning molecular pathways without overall weight loss.

title: MIT study reveals hidden cancer risk in ketogenic diet
summary: MIT researchers found that a ketogenic diet increased small-intestinal tumors in cancer-prone mice through altered intestinal stem cell processing.

summary: Scientists found that prolonged fasting triggers significant physiological changes, with the most notable effects appearing after three days without food.

summary: A ketogenic diet could unlock the metabolic benefits of exercise for people with elevated blood sugar levels.

title: UBC research reveals gender bias gap in exercise physiology studies
summary: A University of British Columbia study finds that exercise physiology research continues to underrepresent women as study subjects and research subjects.

title: Sodium Bicarbonate and Carbohydrate Co-ingestion Improves Athletic Performance When Fatigued
summary: A study from Liverpool John Moores University, in collaboration with World Athletics, found that combining sodium bicarbonate with carbohydrate in a novel energy gel format helps endurance athletes sustain high-intensity efforts during fatigue while causing only mild gastrointestinal discomfort. takeaways: Study tested a new energy gel combining sodium bicarbonate and carbohydrate during three hours of moderate-intensity exercise followed by high-intensity efforts
Sodium bicarbonate ingestion improved performance after prolonged exercise compared to carbohydrate alone

title: Vitamin D2 supplements may reduce natural vitamin D3 levels, study finds
summary: Research warns that taking vitamin D2 supplements can paradoxically lower the body's naturally-produced vitamin D3 levels.

title: Creatine supplementation increases lean muscle and strength in middle-aged adults even without exercise

When combined with resistance training and a calorie-reduced diet, creatine produced significantly greater strength improvements and
takeaways: Non-exercise group taking creatine gained ~2.4 pounds of lean tissue over 12 weeks
Creatine + exercise group showed greater leg press and bench press strength gains than exercise alone
Creatine + exercise + calorie deficit added ~3 pounds lean tissue while reducing body fat percentage
Study involved 64 healthy adults ages 45–65 over 12 weeks

title: Creatine supplementation builds muscle mass in middle-aged adults even without structured exercise
summary: A 12-week study from Texas A&M University found that middle-aged adults (45–65) taking creatine gained approximately 2.4 pounds of lean tissue and increased strength without following a structured exercise program. When combined with exercise and calorie restriction, creatine produced even greater s
takeaways: Adults ages 45–65 taking 10 grams of creatine daily gained roughly 2.4 pounds of lean tissue over 12 weeks without exercise
Creatine combined with resistance training three times per week and calorie deficit resulted in nearly 3 pounds of lean tissue gain while losing fat mass
The study involved 64 healthy adults and was led by Dr. Richard Kreider at Texas A&M's Exercise and Sport Nutrition Lab

title: Curcumin Stands Out Among Five Natural Compounds Tested on Cancer Cells
summary: A study comparing five natural compounds found curcumin most effective at disrupting cancer cell energy production and halting division while sparing healthy muscle cells.
